description: Ground-up fairness overhaul of hask-redis-mux vs StackExchange.Redis benchmarks: convert C# to async/await, fix Haskell PING bypass, clarify pipeline methodology, fix REST server, add memory context, handle missing data gracefully, and add architectural narrative

userStories.title: Convert C# raw benchmark to async Redis calls
userStories.description: As a benchmark author, I need the C# benchmark to use async/await for all Redis operations so that StackExchange.Redis is tested idiomatically (the way it's designed to be used in production).
acceptanceCriteria: All sync Redis calls in Program.cs are replaced with async equivalents: db.PingAsync(), db.StringGetAsync(), db.StringSetAsync(), db.KeyDeleteAsync()
RunBenchmark method is async, uses Task.Run with async lambdas instead of Parallel.For with sync lambdas
Each concurrent task uses 'await' for Redis calls — no .Result or .GetAwaiter().GetResult() blocking
Main method is async (static async Task Main)
Pre-population loop uses StringSetAsync with await
Thread count (Environment.ProcessorCount), warmup (10%), wall-clock throughput, and per-op Stopwatch latency measurement are preserved
JSON output schema is unchanged: {operation: {p50_us, p95_us, p99_us, ops_per_sec, iterations}}
Program builds with 'dotnet build' inside nix-shell
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This is the highest-impact fairness fix. StackExchange.Redis sync methods internally do async+block, causing thread pool starvation under Parallel.For. The async pattern: var tasks = Enumerable.Range(0, NumThreads).Select(t => Task.Run(async () => { await db.StringGetAsync(...); })); await Task.WhenAll(tasks); Use Stopwatch around each await for per-op timing.

userStories.title: Convert C# raw benchmark pipeline test to async
userStories.description: As a benchmark author, I need the pipeline_100_gets benchmark in C# to also use async Redis calls within CreateBatch for consistency.
acceptanceCriteria: The pipeline_100_gets benchmark uses batch.StringGetAsync() (already async by nature of CreateBatch)
batch.Execute() is called, then await Task.WhenAll(tasks) collects results
The batch benchmark is wrapped in the same async RunBenchmark pattern as other operations
Pipeline benchmark still measures the same thing: send 100 GETs in one batch, wait for all responses
JSON output for pipeline_100_gets has same schema as before
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: CreateBatch already returns Task<RedisValue> from StringGetAsync, so the change is minimal — just ensure the outer RunBenchmark is async and the action lambda is async.

userStories.title: Fix Haskell PING to use cluster client
userStories.description: As a benchmark author, I need the Haskell PING benchmark to go through the cluster client (run) instead of raw submitToNode, so it uses the same abstraction level as all other operations.
acceptanceCriteria: PING benchmark calls 'run' with a ping command through ClusterCommandClient, same as SET/GET/DEL
The masterNodes, muxPool, pingCmd, and submitToNode special-case code is removed from Main.hs
The topology/masterNodes/encodeCommandBuilder imports are removed if no longer needed
If 'ping' is not available as a typed command in RedisCommands, use executeCommand ["PING"] through the cluster client
PING benchmark still measures latency and throughput with same iteration count (10000)
JSON output for ping has same schema as before
Program builds with 'cabal build' inside nix-shell
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Check if Database.Redis exports a 'ping' command. If not, use executeCommand. The key insight: currently Haskell PING bypasses cluster routing (topology, MOVED/ASK) giving it an unfair ~3x latency advantage over C# db.Ping() which goes through full ConnectionMultiplexer. Remove imports: Control.Concurrent.STM (readTVarIO), Data.Map.Strict, and the topology-related code.

userStories.title: Rename Haskell pipeline benchmark to sequential_100_gets
userStories.description: As a reader, I need the benchmark names to honestly reflect what each library is doing, since Haskell does 100 sequential GETs while C# does true client-side pipelining.
acceptanceCriteria: In Main.hs, rename 'pipeline_100_gets' to 'sequential_100_gets' in the benchmark call
In 06_benchmarks.md.tmpl, add 'sequential_100_gets' to the OPERATIONS list
The template renders both pipeline_100_gets (C# only) and sequential_100_gets (Haskell only) in the comparison table, with the other library's column showing N/A where applicable
Update the pipeline methodology note to explain: C# pipeline_100_gets uses CreateBatch (true pipelining), Haskell sequential_100_gets sends 100 individual GETs through the multiplexer
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The Haskell benchmark uses mapM_ with 100 sequential get calls — each waits for response before sending next. This is NOT pipelining. C# CreateBatch sends all 100 at once. Renaming makes this honest. The OPERATIONS list in the template controls which ops appear in tables.

userStories.title: Fix C# REST server to use async Redis calls
userStories.description: As a benchmark author, I need the C# REST server to use async Redis methods so it doesn't suffer thread pool starvation under load.
acceptanceCriteria: In RestServer/Program.cs, db.StringGet(cacheKey) is replaced with await db.StringGetAsync(cacheKey)
db.StringSet(cacheKey, jsonData, TimeSpan) is replaced with await db.StringSetAsync(cacheKey, jsonData, TimeSpan)
The MapGet handler lambda is marked async: async (string id, HttpContext ctx) => { ... }
RestServer builds with 'dotnet build' inside nix-shell
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The current sync calls cause thread pool starvation in ASP.NET Core, explaining the 11 req/sec throughput and missing cache-hit data. This is a 3-line change but has massive impact on REST benchmark results.

userStories.title: Add managed heap metric to C# benchmark GC stats
userStories.description: As a reader, I need comparable memory metrics between Haskell and C# — currently Haskell reports live heap (4.9MB) while C# reports total process memory (81MB), which are not equivalent.
acceptanceCriteria: C# Program.cs GC stats dict includes 'managed_heap_bytes': GC.GetTotalMemory(true) — this is the managed heap size comparable to Haskell's max_residency_bytes
The existing peak_working_set_bytes is kept (for total process comparison)
JSON output gc section now has both managed_heap_bytes and peak_working_set_bytes
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: GC.GetTotalMemory(true) forces a GC then returns managed heap size. This is the closest C# equivalent to Haskell's max_residency_bytes from RTS -s stats.

userStories.title: Add memory metric context to benchmark template
userStories.description: As a reader, I need the memory comparison section to explain what each metric measures so the numbers aren't misleading.
acceptanceCriteria: In 06_benchmarks.md.tmpl, add explanatory text above or below Section 6c Memory tables
Text explains: Haskell max_residency_bytes = max live heap at any GC point (excludes stack, code, GC working memory)
Text explains: C# peak_working_set_bytes = total process memory (runtime, JIT code, GC regions, stacks); managed_heap_bytes = managed heap only (comparable to Haskell max_residency)
If managed_heap_bytes is present in C# data, render it in the C# memory table
The render_benchmarks() function handles the new managed_heap_bytes field in the memory rendering loop
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Add managed_heap_bytes to the key list in the C# memory rendering section alongside the existing keys. Add a SECTION_6C_CONTEXT string constant with the explanatory markdown.

userStories.title: Replace bare dash placeholders with meaningful N/A text
userStories.description: As a reader, I need missing benchmark data to show a clear explanation instead of bare '-' dashes that look like the library can't perform the operation.
acceptanceCriteria: The _fmt() function in 06_benchmarks.md.tmpl uses default='N/A' instead of default='-'
When rendering REST benchmark tables, if one library has no data, cells show 'N/A' not '-'
If an entire REST scenario (cache_hit or cache_miss) has no data for one library, the table still renders with N/A
No bare '-' appears in any benchmark table in the rendered output
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Simple change to the _fmt() function default parameter. Also check if REST rendering code passes the default through correctly.

userStories.title: Add architectural context narrative after benchmark tables
userStories.description: As a reader, I want a 'Results Analysis' section after the benchmark data that honestly explains where each library excels and the architectural reasons why.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a render_results_analysis() function to 06_benchmarks.md.tmpl that generates a 'Results Analysis' subsection
The analysis compares throughput data and identifies which library wins each category
For operations where SE.Redis wins (e.g., pipelining), explains: dedicated CreateBatch API, optimized async multiplexer
For operations where hask-redis-mux wins (e.g., single-op concurrency), explains: GHC green threads, implicit multiplexing
The narrative is factual and balanced — no marketing language
render_benchmarks() calls render_results_analysis() and appends it after Section 6c/6d
Analysis gracefully handles missing data (skips categories without data)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use the throughput data (ops_per_sec) to determine winners per category. Group operations: single-op (ping/set/get/del), batch (get_10/get_100/get_1000, set_10/set_100/set_1000), pipeline. The function receives haskell_data and csharp_data dicts.

userStories.title: Regenerate comparison output and validate fairness
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to regenerate all comparison output with the fairness fixes applied and validate the results are credible.
acceptanceCriteria: Delete existing comparison/output/comparison.md and comparison/output/comparison.html
Run python3 generate_comparison.py and it produces both output files without errors
comparison.md Section 6a shows SE.Redis with competitive latency numbers (not 3x worse across the board)
comparison.md Section 6d REST shows data for BOTH libraries (no '-' dashes for cache-hit)
comparison.md Section 6c Memory includes explanatory context about metric differences
comparison.md contains a Results Analysis subsection with architectural context
Haskell pipeline benchmark appears as 'sequential_100_gets' (not 'pipeline_100_gets')
comparison.html renders with all Chart.js charts populated
No temporary build artifacts left after generation
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Ensure Docker Redis cluster is running before regeneration. Use 'nix-shell shell.nix --run "python3 hask-redis-mux/comparison/generate_comparison.py"' to run with all toolchains available. If SE.Redis still loses every metric after async conversion, investigate further — the goal is honest results, not artificially balanced ones.
